key_insight: AutoSynthesis is an end-to-end multi-agent system that automates the most time-consuming parts of meta-analysis from a natural-language research question. It aims to turn evidence synthesis into a scalable, repeatable workflow rather than a largely manual process.
problem_solved: Quantitative evidence synthesis is slow, labor-intensive, and hard to scale because researchers must manually search literature, screen studies, assess eligibility, and extract data.
method: Takes a research question in natural language and converts it into a structured search strategy.
Uses multiple agents to retrieve literature, screen candidate studies, and assess full-text eligibility.
Extracts information needed for meta-analysis in an automated pipeline, supporting end-to-end evidence synthesis.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this could dramatically reduce the effort needed to build literature reviews and evidence summaries for new methods or applications. It may also improve reproducibility and make large-scale meta-analysis more accessible across research domains.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing the flow from research question to final meta-analysis
Multi-agent workflow illustration with separate roles for search, screening, eligibility, and extraction
Before/after comparison of manual vs. automated evidence synthesis timelines
Icon set for literature search, document screening, data extraction, and summary output
paper_title: AutoSynthesis: An agentic system for automated meta-analysis
paper_authors: Moein Taherinezhad, Sebastian Maier, Gerardo Vitagliano, Francesco Pierri, Stefan Feuerriegel
